subject: general
question: How did Public Interest Litigation (PIL) emerge in India as a tool of judicial activism?

options.text: It originated under the 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976).
It was introduced by the Lok Adalat system in 2005.
It began in 1979 when the Supreme Court allowed individuals to file cases for public interest.
It was first used during the Emergency (1975-77).

solution:
The correct answer is __**It began in 1979 when the Supreme Court allowed individuals to file cases for public interest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India was pioneered under judicial activism to provide access to justice for marginalized and underrepresented groups.
 
• The concept gained prominence in 1979 when the Supreme Court allowed individuals or organizations to file cases on behalf of those who were unable to approach the court themselves.
 
• Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer played a significant role in institutionalizing PIL in India, transforming it into a powerful tool for addressing systemic issues.
 
• PIL allows courts to address broader social issues such as environmental protection, human rights violations, corruption, and governmental accountability.
 
• Some landmark PIL cases include the Vishaka Guidelines (against sexual harassment at the workplace) and the Oleum Gas Leak case (which established the principle of absolute liability).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976)**

 
 
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment is known as the "Mini Constitution" and was enacted during the Emergency in 1976.
 
• It introduced changes aimed at strengthening the central government, including the insertion of the words "Socialist" and "Secular" in the Preamble.
 
 
 
• **Lok Adalat **
 
 
• The Lok Adalat system is a mechanism for resolving disputes through conciliation and arbitration outside regular courts.
 
• It was introduced in India under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
